clue.text: Pronouncement of rule that could stop play going on

definitions.text: that could stop play going on

indicators.note: a pronouncement is something spoken, so the word for rule is to be heard rather than written

parts.note: to rule is to reign; a monarch's reign is their rule

explanation.surface: Someone announces a regulation that could halt a game in progress.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, wet weather famously halts the match, hence 'rain stopped play'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet weather is the classic cause of a halted cricket or tennis match, so it is something that could stop play.

clue.text: Excitement of captain rising around happy hour

indicators.note: around tells us the captain's name goes round the other piece
in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: Ahab is the captain in Moby-Dick

indicators.note: happy can mean tipsy, so the letters of the next word stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A ship's master gets excited when happy hour comes round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happy' is used in its sense of tipsy, which makes it a fair signal for jumbling letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy fuss or commotion, a state of public excitement.

clue.text: It's available from the Royal Society and from official sources, too

indicators.note: available from says the letters can be obtained from inside the following words

explanation.surface: Something can be got from a learned society and from official channels as well.
explanation.walkthrough: It is a double hidden clue: the same letters also sit inside 'official sources', so 'and from official sources' repeats the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in addition, as well; a simple synonym.

clue.text: Chance minimal change in New York, bringing in detectives

indicators.note: bringing in means the detectives are taken inside the other word

parts.note: a cent is the smallest US coin, so one cent is minimal change for a New Yorker
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: A small alteration happens by luck in New York once the police get involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'minimal change' is one US cent, the smallest coin a New Yorker carries; CID is the British police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is something that happens by chance, without design.

clue.text: Quartet vying for contracts, top journalist reported

parts.note: North, East, West and South are the four players competing in contract bridge
ED is short for editor, the senior journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: Four companies bidding for business were written up by a leading reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge players are named by compass points, so the four give N, E, W, S.
explanation.definitionFit: To news something is an old verb meaning to report or spread it as tidings.

clue.text: Moving in emergency, scary for Cockneys?

indicators.note: Cockneys famously drop the H at the start of words, so the initial H goes

parts.note: something hair-lifting is frightening enough to make the hair stand up

explanation.surface: A frightening emergency evacuation as described by East Londoners.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are working-class Londoners whose accent drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Airlifting is transporting people or supplies by aircraft, typically in an emergency.

clue.text: Element producing revulsion, added to sulphur

indicators.note: added to says the revulsion word is joined after the sulphur symbol

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
odium is general hatred or disgust

explanation.surface: A chemical element smells so foul when mixed with sulphur that it disgusts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium is a chemical element, a soft reactive metal.

clue.text: Like no ruddy appearance from a cast

parts.note: to cast is to throw, as is to shy

explanation.surface: An actor in a cast looks anything but rosy-cheeked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' suggests actors; here it is a throw, as in a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ashy is ashen and pale, the opposite of a ruddy complexion.

clue.text: Girl that has first date after three months

definitions.text: that has first date after three months
definitions.meaning: the month whose first day comes after January, February and March

explanation.definitionFit: It is a common girl's name and the fourth month of the year.

clue.text: Not able to learn? Can, in special course

indicators.note: in says the can goes inside the rearranged letters
special suggests the letters are given a different, unusual order

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A remedial class offers a can-do special course for slow learners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb but is a tin; the answer is one of the theme's rearrangements of the answer at 27.
explanation.definitionFit: Cretinous means very stupid, so unable to learn anything, which the question mark makes jokey.

clue.text: New outcries agitated obsessive types

indicators.note: agitated means the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Fresh shouts of protest disturbed anxious people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' rearranges OUTCRIES as EUROTICS. Another anagram of the theme answer at 27.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurotic people are anxious and given to obsessive behaviour.

clue.text: Did lie about it? Not ministers!

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: lay is the past tense of lie, so it means did lie

explanation.surface: An accusation of lying answered by the retort that the speakers are not clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer hides an anagram of ITALY, one of the twelve theme countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The laity are ordinary church members as opposed to the clergy, those who are not ministers.

clue.text: Learner driver's supporter holding one down

indicators.note: holding says the supporter contains the other piece

parts.note: in golf the ball sits on a tee when struck with a driver
refers to the answer at 1 down

explanation.surface: A learner driver's backer keeps someone low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' is the golf club, not a motorist; 'one down' is the cross-reference to 1 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone being trained, a learner.

clue.text: Understood that Araucaria's clues involve trickery, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means take the leading letters of these words

explanation.surface: It is a given that the famous setter Araucaria's clues are full of trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria was a renowned Guardian setter, a tribute here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is implied and understood without being stated.

clue.text: Friends are like this in novel, not otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means the letters are arranged in another way

explanation.surface: In a book, the characters are anything but friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: Friends here are Quakers, the Religious Society of Friends, known for pacifism.
explanation.definitionFit: Quakers are committed pacifists, so peaceable and opposed to force is how they are.

clue.text: Delay over a minute as bad speaker?

indicators.note: over means the delay word covers and encloses the other pieces

parts.note: to defer is to delay

explanation.surface: A speaker running a minute over time is a poor one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad speaker' means one who speaks ill of others, not a poor orator.
explanation.definitionFit: A defamer speaks badly of others, damaging their reputation with slander.

clue.text: Dance with drink for sailors one set up

parts.note: rum is a spirit, the traditional naval drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are raised, read upward

parts.note: an AB is one of the sailors, an able seaman

explanation.surface: A dance with grog for the crew, one organised by a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: AB, short for able seaman, is crossword shorthand for a sailor; in a down clue 'set up' reads it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Restrain third man outside hospital

indicators.note: outside means the man goes round the hospital letter

parts.note: Cain, son of Adam and Eve, was the third human in Genesis
H is the abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

explanation.surface: Hold back the third man waiting outside the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third man' evokes the film or a cricket position; it is Cain, the third person after Adam and Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: To chain someone is to fetter them, to restrain them.

clue.text: Male leader of run-of-the-mill trio

definitions.meaning: the first of ..., Dick and Harry, a phrase for ordinary people

explanation.definitionFit: It means a male cat and heads the phrase for any ordinary people.

clue.text: Noble putting a king and queen in disarray

indicators.note: in means the royal pieces go inside the disarray word

parts.note: a mess is a state of disorder
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An aristocrat throws a king and queen into confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disarray' looks like an anagram signal but is MESS, which holds A, R and QU.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquess is a nobleman ranking above an earl and below a duke.

clue.text: I had isolated part of the UK, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
IOM is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Someone says they once had a remote corner of Britain, figuratively.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is strictly a Crown dependency, but the surface lumps it with the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a turn of phrase or way of expressing something.

clue.text: I will bound across motorway at a bad moment

indicators.note: across means the bound word stretches over the motorway letter

parts.note: tied means bound
M is used for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A pedestrian vows to dash across a motorway at the wrong time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' suggests leaping, but it is TIED, round M.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-timed means happening at an inappropriate or unlucky moment.

clue.text: More emotional, calling for attention in bank

indicators.note: in means attention is placed inside the bank word

parts.note: a tier is a row or bank, as of seats
to give an ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Someone more upset is pleading for notice at the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is a row, not a lender. The answer hides an anagram of ERITREA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearier means more inclined to weep, so more emotional.

clue.text: Addition to standard appellation chap put up in time

indicators.note: in means the reversed chap goes inside the time word

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the letters read upward

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: An extra name for a fellow is bestowed in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns MAN into NAM.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnomen-style agname is an extra name added to a person's usual name, like a nickname or epithet.

clue.text: Covered anew, having studied outside class

indicators.note: outside means the studied word goes round the class letters

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
CL is an abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: Freshly clad after taking a course outside school.
explanation.definitionFit: Reclad means given a new covering or cladding, as of a building.

clue.text: Actual things, including good monarch's trappings

indicators.note: including means the actual things word holds the good letter

parts.note: realia are real objects, used in teaching

explanation.surface: Real objects, among them a fine ruler's finery.
explanation.walkthrough: REALIA is a term for real-life objects used as teaching aids. The answer hides an anagram of ALGERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the emblems and robes of royalty, such as crown and sceptre.

clue.text: Enclosure, a pound used for punishment

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A pound, an enclosure for stray animals, is used as a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer hides an anagram of NEPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Penal describes what relates to or is used as punishment, as in a penal colony.

clue.text: Neat and clean

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: unmixed, like neat whisky, and unsoiled or uncontaminated.

clue.text: States altered in 10, 11 and 12 other answers

definitions.text: States altered in 10, 11 and 12 other answers

parts.words: States altered in 10, 11 and 12 other answers
parts.note: the answers at 10 and 11 are rearrangements of this word, and twelve other answers are rearranged national names

explanation.surface: A note that nations appear jumbled in several entries.
explanation.walkthrough: Twelve other answers are anagrams of nations: RAIN (Iran), ALSO (Laos), NEWSED (Sweden), LAITY (Italy), CHAIN (China), PENAL (Nepal), ENEMY (Yemen), REGALIA (Algeria), RUMBA (Burma), PURE (Peru), TEARIER (Eritrea).
explanation.definitionFit: States in the sense of nations are what the twelve rearranged answers conceal.

clue.text: Piles of sand, originally, in river

definitions.meaning: golfers once teed off from small heaps of sand

explanation.definitionFit: Golf tees were originally made from small mounds of sand, and the Tees is an English river.

clue.text: For example, Southern states

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example

explanation.surface: Take the American South, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Southern states' suggests the US South; 'states' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To state is to say, declare something.

clue.text: Servant and I breaking some horses for East Europeans

indicators.note: breaking means the servant and I split the horses word apart

parts.note: roans are horses with mixed-colour coats
a man is a manservant

explanation.surface: A stable hand and I tame some horses for people from eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' suggests taming horses; it puts MANI inside ROANS.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Romania are East Europeans.

clue.text: Some party men expelled after backing the opposition

indicators.note: backing means the selected letters are read in reverse
some says only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A few party members thrown out after supporting the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters YMENE inside 'party men expelled' read backwards; 'backing' looks like support. It also hides YEMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The enemy is the opposing side in a conflict.
